question: Why does too much salt make your cells lose water?
answer: Water follows the salt. Salt outside raises the osmotic pressure, so water crosses the membrane out of the cell. The cell dries and shrinks. That is why drinking seawater dehydrates you.
move: More salt outside pulls water out of your cells by osmosis.
